question: Do the area's published persistent-heat cells correspond to mapped brick kilns?

firms_layer.note: 0.01° cells that FIRMS science-quality data attributes mainly to static sources (type 1–3: volcano, other static land source, offshore). The Dhaka layer of this class was checked against two independent kiln inventories (data/validation/kilns_dhaka-kilns.json); it does not land on mapped kilns more often than randomly placed cells of the same number would, so the class is a persistent-heat proxy, not a kiln inventory.

inventory.name: APAD / IGP asset-data-igp: Bangladesh brick kilns (Brick_kilns_BAN_coal.csv)

method.test: placement test: observed cells versus random cells of the same number in the same bbox

verdict: The published persistent-heat cells do not coincide with the mapped kilns better than randomly placed cells of the same number would. The static layer is a persistent-heat proxy, not a kiln inventory, and must not be read as confirmed kilns.
limitations: The APAD inventory is an asset list with modelled attributes and positions; it is not field-verified ground truth and it is not FIRMS truth either.
A match inside one radius does not identify what the heat source is; the two sources can coincide without one causing the other.
FIRMS detections in this area are sparse and concentrated, so the static layer is a small sample of the area's heat sources.
A negative result here does not prove that no kilns are detected; it shows that this published layer cannot be called a kiln inventory.
